body:
FORMAL UX / ACCESSIBILITY / VISUAL REVIEW — BLOCK

Reviewer: codex-mockup-ux-review
Candidate: cand-5PJBR2B9EXMNW1750DJJ0K0PFY
Commit: 343aa6257ab0f718eb275780714dd31b48d0928b
Base: 003f12b21e1b9793fea479e104c2e2eff3e55fe5
Artifact digest: 2cff910ec709065a38feb64d8e1f5f9c575eb4ec9286b0ad3557437ad8141005

Method: read-only inspection of all 13 indexed PNG plates at original resolution, their frozen HTML twins, the editable sources, the brief, fixture notes, proof boundary and manifest. I also inspected the renderer benchmark plate. No file was edited or staged. The in-app browser could not be started because its installed client resolves a removed prior plugin path; I did not attach to or start another browser. The findings below are direct file and visual findings and do not depend on a live-browser inference.

WHAT PASSES AS DESIGN DIRECTION

- Main and Compact establish the intended hierarchy: persistent Codex, exactly one replaceable primary projection, and a genuinely collapsible inspector. Main gives the Codex about 44 percent of working width; Compact preserves it and collapses the inspector.
- The normal channel budget is explicit and credible: one hierarchy lane, one context lane, one docked quantitative feature, with the other channels named but unpainted.
- Selection, keyboard focus and epistemic role are separated by outline, dash, edge, text and position. The grayscale and dichromat plate is unusually strong; no scientific state relies on hue alone.
- Reflow is the right conceptual response: exact text grows, the two-dimensional projection becomes pannable with a table counterpart, and the inspector becomes a disclosure without dropping fields.
- Motion is well resolved. The 0 ms reduced-motion treatment preserves breadcrumb, tether, ghost and announcement; it is not merely a faster animation.
- The state vocabulary is scientifically careful: present, zero, missing, not requested, unauthorised, low coverage, unresolved, off-source, unranked, stale, on-mark, via-ancestor, off-projection, reader horizon, multimodal alignment, distortion, named off-source destinations, omission, misordering, privacy block, loading, no data, no accepted episode, long labels and long work remain distinct.
- The source, recall and interview screens no longer fabricate War of the Ghosts evidence. The dominant synthetic label, synthetic namespaces, explicit uncalibrated scores and proof boundary are major improvements.
- PROOF-BOUNDARY.md correctly says that the plates do not prove live keyboard, reflow, motion, privacy, export or provider behavior. That boundary must remain.

BLOCKERS ON THIS EXACT CANDIDATE

UX-B1 — The frozen HTML presents dead controls and contradicts its own focus-order plate.

Every frozen plate has zero scripts. Nonetheless main.html contains 19 elements with tabindex=0 and role=button, recall-matrix.html contains 12, and interview-mode.html contains 13. They are inert. The source and recall rows, projection selectors, level controls, horizon and inspector controls therefore enter the review tab order but cannot activate. FocusOrder says the whole instrument has twelve tab stops and that each projection is one composite tab stop; the frozen Main plate alone exceeds that count before ordinary links. This is not merely missing runtime proof: the portable HTML review artifact itself asserts false button semantics.

Resolve one of two ways: make frozen plates explicitly static and remove role=button, tabindex, aria-pressed, pointer cursors and other active semantics; or provide the required interaction prototype with real native controls and the declared composite focus behavior. Every direct plate also needs a visible FROZEN DESIGN SPECIFICATION — CONTROLS ARE INERT label. The current synthetic watermark says that data are invented; it does not say that controls are nonfunctional.

All 13 standalone plate HTML files also lack html lang, title and viewport metadata. The index has these, but a directly opened plate does not. A portable standalone review surface needs them.

UX-B2 — The proposed SVG accessibility model is internally incompatible.

FocusOrder states both that every SVG figure has role="img" and that marks inside it form a roving-tabindex group. An image role is a black-box accessible object whose descendants are presentational in platform accessibility mappings; it cannot safely own interactive descendant marks. Choose and specify one coherent composite pattern: for example, an outer labelled group with a single focusable owner and aria-activedescendant into a DOM list or grid twin while the SVG is inert, or individually exposed SVG marks under a non-image group. Do not promise both role=img flattening and descendant focus.

The generic arrow contract also does not define matrix navigation. The recall and interview matrices need explicit row, column, cell, off-source and unranked movement semantics. Finally, J, K, N, P, I, slash, brackets and G then O are character-only shortcuts. WCAG 2.1.4 requires that such shortcuts be scoped to a focused component, switchable, or remappable. Pointer equivalents do not satisfy that requirement. Record the scope and escape behavior before engineering handoff.

UX-B3 — The exact-text typography regresses in the two recall modes and contradicts the token sheet.

Tokens specifies exact text at mono 16 / 24.8. Main and Compact honor it. RecallMatrix renders the source Codex at 12 px / 1.4 and exact participant rows at 11 px / 13 px with two-line clamping. InterviewMode renders participant transcript at 12.5 px and exact detail rows at 11 px / 12.5 px. At 1536 × 1024 the known-source Codex occupies only 300 px, while the matrix is dominant; exact story and recall words are again the material sacrificed to density.

Keep dense matrix row labels only as summaries if needed, but provide the persistent exact source and exact recall rails at the declared reading token. The selected inspector is not a substitute for readable access to every observational unit. Interview transcript text should use the same exact-text token. This was a central v1 defect and remains acceptance-critical.

UX-B4 — Compact silently drops exact text, and the clipping court cannot detect it.

Compact contains only s01 through the first line of s06. Sentences s07 through s10 are absent from its DOM, the Codex body uses overflow:hidden, no scroll or continuation affordance is shown, and the footer says Page 1 of 1. That is content loss, not a compact viewport. The outer-artboard overflow court passes because the omitted content never crosses the artboard; it cannot prove internal reachability.

Include the complete text in a scrollable Codex, show truthful pagination or continuation, and add an internal-content reachability check. Page 1 of 1 may not accompany a partial source.

UX-B5 — One required edge-state family is still absent.

StateBoard is excellent on missing, unresolved, empty and loading states, but it does not show a provider or compilation failure separate from loading, no data and stale receipt. Deliverable 11 explicitly requires errors and loading. Add a compilation/provider error state that reserves no fabricated partial value, names the failed stage, exposes a receipt or diagnostic reference, and provides a recovery or retry path. Keep it distinct from a valid no-data result and from a stale-but-previously-compiled view.

UX-B6 — Two labels overstate evidence even inside the synthetic fixture.

Main and Compact label the basis and footer researcher-reviewed narrative acceptance fixture, but FIXTURE-NOTES describes internally consistent inventions and records no independent review receipt. The global synthetic watermark reduces the risk but does not make a fabricated review status a good exemplar. Use synthetic design fixture — not admitted or researcher-reviewed, or bind a real review receipt.

NON-BLOCKING HANDOFF NOTES

- The proof boundary is honest, but the brief still lists an interactive prototype as required deliverable 12 and leaves every acceptance checkbox open. Either deliver that prototype later or state explicitly in the brief that this candidate intentionally closes only the static-design package.
- Main, Reflow, FocusOrder, Grayscale, Motion and StateBoard should be retained substantially as drawn after the blockers above are repaired.
- Known-source Recall should preserve the matrix-first decision. The fix is not to replace it with ribbons; it is to restore readable exact rails and define a lawful keyboard composite.
- The direct visual review found no outer-artboard clipping, no color-only scientific state, and no reduced-motion loss of meaning. The Compact internal truncation is the exception and is precisely why outer-bound checks are insufficient.

Formal disposition: BLOCK this exact SHA. A successor can be narrow: correct static HTML semantics and plate labels, fix the focus composite and shortcut specification, restore exact-text sizing and Compact reachability, add the missing error state, and remove the unsupported researcher-reviewed label. This review does not authorize, land, push or approve any runtime or Intaglio change.
